A builder roof that failed early, a 1980s roof on its last legs, or shingles torn loose by a spring storm. One free call, any hour, puts you through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Cypress calls.

Cypress is a place with no city limits

Roofing in Cypress, TX starts with a fact many newcomers miss: there is no City of Cypress. The name covers a wide, unincorporated swath of northwest Harris County, served by the county, the school district and a patchwork of utility districts, and it has no municipal building department of its own.

The name itself shows how the area grew. Cy-Fair comes from the 1930s merger of the Big Cypress school and Fairbanks High School into one district, and for decades the land around them stayed rural. Then the subdivisions arrived in waves, first along Highway 6 and FM 529, later out along US 290 and the Grand Parkway. That is why one Cypress street can hold a house on its third roof and the next can hold a roof that has seen only a few summers.

Houston Expert Roofers builds no roofs anywhere. It is a phone number that answers itself: the call is picked up by an automated assistant, which learns what the roof is doing and hands you to an independent, locally owned roofing company that works in Cypress. That company does the looking, the pricing and the roofing, and it bills you directly.

Calls from Cypress cluster around a few problems. Wind damage after a squall line, leaks on newer houses that trace back to a single detail, and replacement quotes on houses old enough that the first roof went on in the 1980s. May 16, 2024: the evening Cypress lost its roofs

Most of greater Houston remembers that Thursday for the derecho downtown. In Cypress it also brought tornadoes. Here is the sequence, drawn from National Weather Service findings as reported by ABC13 and KHOU.

  1. Early evening, a tornado touches down. The weather service's survey team rated it an EF-1 with peak winds of 110 mph. Its path ran about 0.77 miles and reached up to 100 yards across.
  2. A 55 and over community takes a beating. ABC13 reported significant storm damage at The Heritage at Towne Lake, a 55 and over community, where neighbors spent the next days cleaning up torn roofing and debris.
  3. The same storm crosses the whole metro. The weather service's Houston/Galveston office documented a swath of winds above 100 mph through the Houston area that night, the event now called the May 2024 derecho.
  4. Three months later, a second Cypress tornado. On August 13, 2024, after reviewing video, the weather service confirmed that another EF-1 had touched down that evening in the Bridgeland area, according to KHOU.
  5. Seven weeks after the derecho, Beryl. Hurricane Beryl came ashore near Matagorda on July 8, 2024 and left more than two million CenterPoint Energy customers without power across the region, a second round of tropical wind on roofs that had just been through May.

The lesson for a Cypress roof is that wind damage is often partial. A house a few streets from a tornado path can lose seal strips and ridge caps without anything obvious from the curb, and the first sign may be a ceiling stain in the next heavy rain. If your roof went through 2024 and nobody has looked at it closely since, that is worth a call. Many roofers inspect at no charge; confirm that on the call.

Two generations of Cypress roofs, two different first calls

Where your house sits in Cypress history changes who you should call first. Two well documented communities show the range.

An early Cy-Fair subdivision such as CopperfieldA newer community such as Bridgeland
When it beganDevelopers bought about 1,800 acres at Highway 6 and FM 529 in 1977, and the first homes sold roughly two years later. Building continued into the 1990s.Most of the land was bought in 2003 and new home sales began in 2006. With a later purchase it now covers about 11,500 acres with more than 3,000 acres of lakes, trails and parks.
Where the roof likely standsMany houses are on a second or later roof, and some may carry an overlay on top of an older layer.Many roofs are originals from the builder, some only a few seasons old.
Paperwork to find firstReceipts or a contract from the last re-roof, and any record of layers.The builder's written warranty, the closing papers, and the shingle maker's warranty terms.
The question to put to a rooferWill you tear off to the deck, and what is your written price per sheet for rotten decking?Is this a storm claim, an installation problem the builder or shingle maker should look at, or wear?

A young roof that leaks is a warranty question first

When a roof fails in its first few years, the cause is usually one detail done badly, not shingles that wore out. That changes the order of calls. Read the builder warranty that came with the house, note what it covers and for how long, and look up the shingle maker's warranty, which may depend on how the roof was installed. A roofer who works Cypress should ask the age of the house before quoting and tell you plainly if the builder ought to see the roof first.

An older roof is a decking question

On a house that has been reroofed before, what matters most is underneath. A second layer laid over the first hides soft decking and makes the next replacement heavier work. Ask for photos of the bare deck once the old layers are off, before new underlayment covers it. Those photos are often the only record of what was found, because no city inspector stands in the driveway in Cypress.

Permits, the county and your HOA

With no city, building permits in Cypress come from Harris County, through the engineer's office. Its permits FAQ links the need for a permit to development and gives that word a very wide meaning that takes in buildings and almost any other change made to a property. Its online application list covers residential construction. What its pages do not do is address re-roofing by name, so this page will not tell you a replacement is exempt or that it is not. If you want certainty for your address, ask the county's permits office directly, and have the roofer write into the contract which permits, if any, it will pull.

In practice the rule book most Cypress homeowners meet is the one from their homeowners association. Master-planned communities usually require architectural approval for a change of roof color or material, and a replacement in a different shade is a change. Texas Property Code section 202.011 stops an association from prohibiting impact-resistant or energy-saving shingles that look like the ones it already permits, which is useful in a part of the county where spring storms bring hail. A 1.25 inch hail report near Cypress on December 24, 2024, listed in StormerSite's log compiled from weather service reports, is a reminder that it is not only a spring problem.

Cypress is well inland, outside the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area, so no TDI windstorm inspection applies to a roof here.

Why Cypress homeowners call the line

Nobody else is checking

Without a city building department, the contract and the roofer's own photos are what protect you. Starting with a company that answers the phone and works this side of the county is a reasonable first step, and you are free to get a second written quote.

The tornado streets are still being sorted out

Two confirmed tornadoes in one evening, then Beryl, is a lot for one part of the county. A house near Towne Lake or Bridgeland that never had a close look after May 16 may still have loose seal strips or creased shingles that only show from up close, and owners want someone to look before the next wet season.

Builder roofs reaching their first storms

Every year more Cypress houses go from new to lived in. When a young roof leaks, owners want someone who can say whether it looks like wear, wind or an installation miss, so they know whether to call the builder, the insurer or neither.

Big trees over older roofs

The older Cy-Fair sections have grown tall pines and oaks. Shade keeps moss and debris on the shingles, and limbs come down in tropical wind. When a limb is lying on the roof, keep clear of it and of any wires it touched, and let the roofer handle it.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Questions to ask a roofer working in Cypress

  • Which permits, if any, will you pull for this address with Harris County, and will you put that in writing?
  • Will you prepare the HOA architectural submittal, and which colors does my section allow?
  • After the May 2024 storms, did you check for broken seal strips and creased shingles, and can I see your photos?
  • If my house is under ten years old, do you think the builder or shingle maker should see this first?
  • Will you tear off every existing layer, and what is your written price per sheet of decking?
  • Can your insurer send me a certificate of liability insurance directly?
  • What workmanship warranty do you give in writing, and will you register the shingle maker's warranty for me?

Weigh quotes item by item rather than by the bottom line. The roof replacement cost guide covers what pushes a price up, and the roof lifespan guide helps you judge whether an older Cypress roof is near the end.

How a call from Cypress works

  1. Call the numberAn automated assistant answers (832) 662-4107 at any hour and asks which service you need, since the line also takes heating, cooling, pressure washing and water damage calls.
  2. Describe the roofA leak, missing shingles, hail, a limb on the roof or an old roof you want looked at, plus your part of greater Houston and how urgent it is.
  3. Get put throughYour call is transferred to an independent, locally owned roofing company, which hears a short summary before it picks up.
  4. Deal with the roofer directlyIt inspects, quotes and does the work, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it misses the call, it gets your name, number, city and need to call you back.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Who are good roofing companies in Cypress, TX?

This page will not rank or name any, because it has no way to judge them and Texas has no state roofing license to look up. A better test is what a company hands you: a certificate of liability insurance sent from its insurer, a written scope that says tear-off or overlay, photos of your own roof, and addresses of Cypress roofs it finished that you can drive past. The guide to checking a roofer lists the rest.

Does a roof replacement in Cypress need a permit?

Cypress has no city hall, so no city permit office exists. Building on unincorporated county land is permitted by the county engineer's office, and its permits FAQ ties permits to development, which it defines very widely: nearly any change people make to land or buildings. Its pages do not single out re-roofing, so ask the county before work starts if you are unsure, and ask the roofer to put its answer in the contract.

My Cypress home is only a few years old. Why is the roof already leaking?

Young roofs usually fail at a detail, not across the whole surface: a pipe boot, a missed nail line, flashing at a wall or a valley. Before anyone tears into it, find your builder's written warranty and the shingle maker's warranty, because both may speak to installation problems. A storm is different: storm damage goes to your homeowners insurer. The roof leak repair page explains how a leak gets traced.

Do roofing contractors in Cypress need my HOA's approval?

In most master-planned Cypress communities the deed restrictions give an architectural committee a say over roof color and material, so plan on it. Texas Property Code section 202.011 limits that power in one way: an association may not ban shingles built to resist wind and hail, or to save energy, when they look like shingles it already allows. Send the committee the exact product and color, and keep its written approval.

Can I call about a storm-damaged roof in Cypress at night?

An automated assistant picks up whatever the hour, asks that you choose roofing, then takes a sentence or two about the damage and your part of Cypress. It transfers you to an independent roofing company that takes calls here; if nobody can answer, your name, number, city, need and urgency are sent for a call back. Stay off the roof meanwhile. The storm damage steps guide covers the first day.
